# `tests/fixtures/assets/3d-templates`

Every file the generator here produces is **original work by Astrum Forge Studios**, released under
the repository's Apache-2.0 licence. Nothing is derived from a third-party model, texture, or sound
pack, and nothing was downloaded.

| File                 | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `make-level-art.mjs` | The generator. It writes straight into `templates/3d-third-person/assets/` and `templates/3d-first-person/assets/`, because a template has to be self-contained: `create-ignifx` copies the directory verbatim. |

Run it with `node tests/fixtures/assets/3d-templates/make-level-art.mjs`. It asserts a 64 KB
per-file ceiling and throws if an image grows past it.

The templates' **sounds** are not written here: every `.wav` in every template is generated by
`tests/fixtures/assets/audio-templates/make-template-audio.mjs`.

## What it writes

| Output                                         | What it is                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `floor.png` (128×128)                          | A poured slab scored into bays, with a seeded speckle so a large `uvScale` still has something to resolve. |
| `wall.png` (128×128)                           | A ribbed panel with a skirting band, so a wall reads which way up it is.                                   |
| `crate.png` (128×128)                          | Planks, a diagonal brace, and a bevelled border. Tinted per template.                                      |
| `sky.png` (256×256)                            | A vertical three-stop gradient, uniform across every row, ordered-dithered on a 4×4 lattice.               |
| `player.glb`, `companion.glb`, `viewmodel.glb` | Copies of `../3d/rig.glb` under the addresses each template needs.                                         |
| `hero.animator.json`                           | A copy of `../3d/hero.animator.json`.                                                                      |

## The sky

`Environment.skybox` wants a `.dds` or `.env` cube map, and neither can be produced here without an
image library, so the sky is `sky.png` on an **inverted sphere** with `sky.material.json` — a `pbr`
material with `unlit: true` and `doubleSided: true`, both of which are real fields of the material
schema (`skills/ignifx/references/formats/ignifx.material.md`).

Because every row of the image is a single colour, its left and right edges are identical and the
seam where the sphere's UVs wrap is invisible. The 4×4 ordered dither is what keeps a gradient that
moves less than one code value per row from banding; the lattice is periodic and 256 is a whole
number of tiles wide, so it too meets itself at the wrap.

The two templates get different skies on purpose: `3d-third-person` a clear late afternoon (a deep
blue zenith through a pale band to a warm horizon), `3d-first-person` a cooler, dimmer,
indoor-adjacent dusk.

## The hand-written material documents

`*.material.json` is authored by hand next to the textures rather than generated — a material is a
handful of factors, not art:

| Document                 | What it is                                                                                          |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `floor.material.json`    | The floor slab, rough and non-metallic.                                                             |
| `wall.material.json`     | The ribbed panel.                                                                                   |
| `crate.material.json`    | The crate, with a little sheen and a very faint tinted `emissive` so it does not go flat in shadow. |
| `sky.material.json`      | Unlit, double-sided, `sky.png` as its base colour.                                                  |
| `emissive.material.json` | An untextured glow for the interaction marker, in each template's accent hue.                       |

## Where the pieces come from

- The PNG encoder is `../2d-templates/png.mjs` — a hand-written PNG chunk writer over `node:zlib`.
  No image library is involved anywhere.
- The rig and its state machine are the Phase 7 fixtures in `../3d/`, generated by `make-rig.mjs`.
  They are **copied** rather than referenced: `create-ignifx` copies a template directory into a
  player's project, so a template cannot point at a path in this repository.
- Two of the copies are the same bytes under two names on purpose. `@ignifx/3d` binds one
  `Animator` per model asset — Babylon Lite binds an animation group to a single manager, and a
  cloned skinned mesh shares the template's skeleton — so the third-person player and its companion
  must load the rig under two different addresses to animate independently.

Every image is deterministic: the noise comes from a seeded generator, so a regenerated file is
byte for byte the file that is committed and a diff in review means a real change.
